answer: Anchor each identity to one distinct parcel in a public land registry: a deed is recorded once, like an ivory tablet in a county archive, and no second identity may claim the same plot. A farmer wanting ten thousand fakes must buy ten thousand parcels, tying up real capital per fake, and each deed passes through the registry's narrow inlet of title checks, so bulk forgery stalls. The thread of ownership stays public, so a duplicated claim is spotted at once; the limit is access, since most agents own no land and need a leasehold or sponsored path.
